gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-mahajan: Noto Sans Mahajani brings a modern lowercase that rises above its capitals, with a funnel-like opening in the e. gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-mono: Noto Sans Mono spaces its letters so generously that nothing ever bumps, and every curve stays open. Disorder, meanwhile, adds the chaos on top, its round bowls holding one outline while its lowercase looms large and scattered above the sans below.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Dense and weighty through the middle, Noto Sans Myanmar reads as a thick band of text with a broad, welcoming c. Over many lines, Noto Sans Myanmar stays firm and sturdy while Disorder, with no swing between thick and thin, supplies the raw edge.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-nabatae: Rough, spaced-out and loud, Disorder draws its diagonals as heavy as its horizontals. Noto Sans Nabataean, with lowercase nearly reaching cap height and sweeping s curves, is the sans-serif anchor that makes the whole pairing feel deliberate.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-nag-mun: Noto Sans Nag Mundari reads with half-unwrapped c and s shapes and a lowercase that rivals its capitals. Disorder adds a rough counterpoint, its curves meeting stems without any swelling, and a larger size for the heading would let that rawness breathe.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-nandina: Disorder is all spaced-out glyphs and untidy attitude, with diagonals drawn as thick as its horizontals. gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-newa: Disorder has joints where strokes meet without thinning or bulging, and it carries a raw, jostling feel. Noto Sans Newa does its best work below, offering a sans with a clearly open e and lowercase bowls that stretch upward.
